sentences.text: Revenue compounded from $6.91 billion in FY2017 [F1] to $216 billion in FY2026 [F10], a 46.6% CAGR [F211].
Growth stalled in FY2023, when revenue rose 0.2% [D284] and operating margin fell 21.6pp [D299], with gross margin down to 56.9% [F27] on $2.17 billion of inventory provisions [P35].
FY2024 revenue grew 125.9% to $60.9 billion [D338][F8], which the filing ties to Data Center growth of 217% on enterprise software and consumer internet demand [P25][D615].
FY2025 added a further 114.2% [D393] before growth slowed to 65.5% in FY2026 [D448].
Data Center products made up 89.7% of FY2026 revenue [D620], up from 78.0% in FY2024 [D614].
Data Center contributed 60.2pp of FY2026's 65.5% revenue growth [D622][D448], with Compute at 46.1pp [D629] and Networking at 14.1pp [D636].
The filing ties this to Blackwell demand, which lifted Data Center computing 58.9% [D628], and to the NVLink and Ethernet and InfiniBand ramp, which lifted networking 141.5% [D635][P8].
Operating income grew 60.1% [D449], slower than revenue's 65.5% [D448], as gross profit grew 56.8% [D460].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% [D452] against net income growth of 64.7% [D450], with diluted shares down 1.2% [D470].

Operating margin was 60.4% in FY2026 [F50], against a window median of 32.8% [D813] and a window low of 15.7% in FY2023 [D811]; that is the 100th percentile of semis peers, whose median is 27.0% [D836][D837].
Operating margin fell 2.0pp [D463] as cost of revenue cut 3.9pp [D477], partly offset by R&D at +1.3pp [D478] and SG&A at +0.6pp [D479].

The cited passages do not explain the FY2026 gross margin decline from 75.0% [F29] to 71.1% [F30]; the 10-K instead ties a $4.5 billion H20 inventory charge to Compute & Networking segment operating income [P7].
The largest window move, FY2024's +38.5pp [D353], included +15.8pp from cost of revenue [D367], which the filing ties to Data Center growth and lower inventory provisions [P20].

Net margin of 55.6% [F70] sits 4.8pp below operating margin [F50], as the effective tax rate rose to 15.1% [D434] from 13.3% [D379] on smaller tax benefits from stock-based compensation and research credits [P2].
Operating cash flow of $103 billion [F100] was 0.86x net income [D435], and free cash flow of $96.7 billion [F110] was 0.81x [D436], against a window median of 0.83x [D828].
Operating cash flow fell 38.1% to $5.64 billion in FY2023 [D289][F97], which the filing ties to the $1.35 billion Arm termination cost and higher tax payments [P29].
Inventory rose 112.3% to $21.4 billion in FY2026 [D474][X222], faster than revenue's 65.5% [D448], and the cited passages do not explain the build.
Capex was 2.8% of revenue [D431] and 2.13x D&A [D437], and the 86.7% rise in capex [D455] has no explanation in the cited passages.
Net cash was $2.14 billion in FY2026 [D441], 1.0% of revenue [D442], against $34.7 billion [D386] and 26.6% [D387] in FY2025.
The FY2026 net cash figure is not comparable, because the pack has no FY2026 short-term investment line, while short-term investments were $34.6 billion in FY2025 [X188].
Net cash as a share of revenue ranks at the 83rd percentile of six semis peers [D844], against a peer median of -13.9% [D845].
Investing outflows reached $52.2 billion [F120], which the filing attributes to higher equity investment purchases and a Groq license [P1].
Buybacks of $40.1 billion [X150] and dividends of $974 million [X160] equalled 42.5% of free cash flow [D444], and diluted shares fell 1.2% [D470].

Customer concentration: two direct customers took 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue, mainly through Compute & Networking [P6], and an indirect customer was estimated at 10% or more of FY2025 revenue [P13].
A few buyers can move the whole revenue line, and the pattern predates FY2026 [P21].
Inventory rose 112.3% to $21.4 billion in FY2026 [D474][X222], and days inventory reached 125 [D446] from 113 in FY2025 [D391].
The FY2023 precedent of $2.17 billion of provisions that cut gross margin to 56.9% [P35][F27] shows how quickly a build can reach margin.
Data-quality flag: diluted share counts jump 303.7% in FY2022 [D251] and 894.5% in FY2025 [D415], so the 7.4% diluted EPS CAGR [F216] spans basis breaks and is not a like-for-like trend.
Gross margin against 71.1% [F30]: a FY2027 10-K reading below 71.1% would confirm that the FY2026 decline [D462] is continuing, while a return to the FY2025 level of 75.0% [F29] would reverse it.

Days inventory against 125 days [D446]: a fall back toward 113 days [D391] would show the build unwinding, while a move above the window high of 162 days [D282] would echo the FY2023 provisions [P35].
Largest direct customer share against 22% [P6]: a FY2027 10-K showing that share below 22% while revenue keeps growing would indicate diversification.
